changes.after: Let a child class supply its own version of an inherited method.

before: class Cat extends Animal inherits from Animal and provides its own implementation of sound(). A variable typed Animal may refer to a Cat object.

@Override asks the compiler to check that a method really overrides an inherited declaration. The matching name and parameter list matter; accidentally adding a parameter would create a different overload.
Calling the overridden instance method uses the actual object type at runtime. This rule is not a claim that fields or static methods have the same dynamic dispatch behavior.

Expected output or behavior: meow
. Compiler evidence is recorded separately from app reading completion.
Optional local transfer task: Add a Dog override and call both through Animal references. You may trace it without a JDK; reading completion is not proof of a local run.
after: Inheritance lets one class build on another. Cat extends Animal makes Cat a child class of Animal. A Cat is also an Animal, so an Animal reference can point to a Cat.

Overriding means supplying a new version of an inherited instance method. @Override asks Java to check that the method really does this. Its inputs must match; changing the inputs can make a separate overload instead.
For an overridden instance method, Java uses the actual object's type to choose the body when the program runs. Fields and static methods do not follow this same rule.
The program prints meow. The reference's declared type is Animal, but it points to a Cat, whose sound method runs.
The quiz creates an Animal object instead. The call stays the same, so focus on which object it reaches.

before.question: Create an Animal instead of a Cat but keep the same variable and call. What prints?
choices: quiet because the actual object is now Animal
meow because the variable once mentioned Cat
Nothing because Animal cannot have methods
before.explanation: This Animal object uses Animal.sound. The reference’s declared type alone did not choose the Cat implementation.

after.question: Use new Animal() instead of new Cat(). What prints?
choices: quiet, because the actual object is now an Animal.
meow, because Cat still exists in the file.
Nothing, because Animal cannot have a method.
after.explanation: The reference now reaches an Animal object, so Animal.sound runs and returns quiet.
